title: Stop reporting delivered Claude Code messages as failed
description:
devhost confirms a Claude Code send only when `--replay-user-messages` echoes it, and gives up after 30 seconds (`chatCallContext`, `chat_sessions.go`; the browser gives up at 45 seconds in `createAgentChatClient.ts`). The echo arrives when Claude Code picks the message up, not when it receives it. A message sent during a long tool call took 43.5 seconds to echo, and one sent during a pending approval took 38.4 seconds, so delivered messages are reported as failed. On timeout `exchange` also removes the pending entry (`chat_process.go`), so a late echo confirms nothing.

A resend is not safe. A second UUID delivers the message twice. The same UUID is dropped silently mid-turn, and after completion it is echoed but nothing runs.

Change:
- When `system/init` advertises `msg_lifecycle_v1`, settle the pending `user:<uuid>` on the `command_lifecycle` `queued` frame for that `command_uuid`.
- Fail the send on `refused`, `discarded` or `cancelled`.
- `command_lifecycle` is internal and missing from the SDK message types. Without the capability, a successful write that times out returns a distinct unconfirmed result, keeps the pending entry so a late echo can settle it, and releases the socket send worker.
- Replace the browser message state with `sending`, `queued`, `started`, `unconfirmed` and `failed`.
- Tell the user to check the conversation before retrying. Retry only on user action, and restore the draft only on a definite failure.

Done when a message sent during a long tool call or a pending approval shows as queued within a second and never as failed, with Go tests covering both the lifecycle path and the fallback. Go tests must not run the machine's `claude`.
